In three days, only 150.5 overs have been bowled. Hard to see this Test getting a result with the forecast on the remaining two days. As of now, New Zealand will keep that aside and aim to bat well tomorrow and set a decent target for the visitors. Pakistan, on the other hand, will aim to bowl well and get the Kiwis all out. Do join us at 0300 IST (2130 GMT, previous day) for all the action from Day 4. Adios! Take Care!

Tim Southee was the star for the home side. He razed Pakistan with a 6-fer. Neil Wagner took 3 wickets while the star in the first Test, de Grandhomme could not take more than a solitary wicket. The hosts were guilty of dropping some simple catches, else they could have been well in control of the game.

Not a bad day for Pakistan. They started at 76/5 but counter-attacking innings from Sarfraz Ahmed and later Sohail Khan kept the Kiwis at bay. Babar Azam held one end with a fine unbeaten 90 and the Kiwis would have hoped for a lead bigger than the eventual 55.

0945 IST UPDATE - I am afraid, that is it. We have had only one ball of the third innings and PLAY HAS BEEN CALLED OFF for the day. With the continuous rain falling and the forecast not pretty, common sense has prevailed.
